AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To explore the effects of maternal high-fat diet induced obesity on fetal growth and the expression of placental nutrient transporters.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Maternal obesity was established in rats by 8 weeks of pre-pregnancy high-fat (HF) diet feeding, while rats in the control group were fed with normal (CON) diet. Diet induced obesity (DIO) rats and diet induced obesity resistant (DIR) rats were selected according to body weight gain over this period. After copulation, the CON rats were divided into two groups: switched to HF diet (CON-HF group) or maintained on the CON diet (CON-CON group). The DIO rats and DIR rats were maintained on the HF diet throughout pregnancy. Pregnant rats were euthanized at day 21 gestation, fetal and placental weights recorded and placental tissue collected. RT-PCR was used to determine mRNA expression of placental nutrient transporters. Protein expression was determined by Western blot.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Average fetal weight of DIO dams was reduced by 6.9% and the placentas of CON-HF and DIO dams were heavier than the placentas of CON-CON and DIR dams at day 21 of gestation. The fetal/placental weight ratio of DIO dams was significantly reduced compared with the fetal/placental weight ratio of CON-CON dams. The mRNA expression of glut-1 and snat-2 were not significantly different between groups. The mRNA and protein expression of CD36, FATP-1 and FATP-4 in DIO dams were decreased significantly.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Maternal obesity induced by a high-fat diet led to intrauterine growth retardation and down-regulated the expression of placental fatty acid transporters.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of maternal obesity on fetal growth and the expression of placental fatty acid transporters.

Journal.Title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
